Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the Sri Lankan openers. South Africa are in a huddle before they disperse. Kusal Perera and Pathum Nissanka will open the innings for Sri Lanka. Lungi Ngidi will start the proceedings with the new ball for South Africa. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, South Africa have a humongous total on the board. Three batters breached the three-figure mark and it will require something similar from Sri Lanka if they are to get over the line here. Can they do the unthinkable? We shall find out when we return in a bit for the chase.

Rassie van der Dussen is in for a chat. He says that it was a perfect outing with the bat. Adds that it swung early on but they worked hard in the middle overs. Tells that Quinton de Kock's batting is unbelievable at times and praises Miller and Markram too. Mentions that they just play according to the conditions and it is hard to say if they will get more 400+ scores. Says that David Miller, Aiden Markram and Heinrich Klaasen are the best hitters and showed that here. Ends by saying that the job is only half done and their bowlers would have learned a thing or two to execute their plans and get the win

As far as Sri Lanka are concerned, it has been a disappointing bowling effort from them. Dilshan Madushanka set the tone early with an early wicket of the South African skipper. His bowling partner, Kasun Rajitha, kept things quiet from the other end with probing lines and lengths. In the middle phase, the spinners and pacers were taken to the cleaners, and not converting half chances did not help Sri Lanka's cause either. Just when the wheels were starting to come off, Matheesha Pathirana got rid of Quinton de Kock before Dunith Wellalage sent Rassie van der Dussen back into the hut 7 overs later. Having dismissed both set batters, Sri Lanka sensed an opening, but they found no answers to the brilliance of Aiden Markram. Towards the end, a slow over-rate penalty crushed any hopes they would have had of finishing strongly with the ball.

South Africa have announced their arrival at the World Cup with a mammoth total! A field day for the Proteas as they end up with the highest total in ODI World Cup history. After they were inserted to bat, skipper Temba Bavuma got himself going with a couple of crisp boundaries before his stay was cut short in the second over. Coming in at number 3, Rassie van der Dussen took his time initially, as did Quinton de Kock. As the innings progressed, both batters grew in confidence and did not shy away from punishing the loose deliveries. Neither de Kock nor van der Dussen struggled and were in complete control on their way to their respective hundreds. What followed was an absolute carnage by Aiden Makram, and he ensured that the South African innings did not lose steam. He unleashed himself all over the park and brought up his century off just 49 balls, the fastest in ODI World Cup history. David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen filled their boots as well in what was a special batting effort from South Africa.

Only a single to end the innings then! Dilshan Madushanka finishes with yet another good yorker, outside off, Marco Jansen reaches for it and forces it down to long off for one more. South Africa finish on 428/5!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! The bell has been rung as per tradition on this ground. Sri Lankan players are spreading out to take their respective field positions. Quinton de Kock and Temba Bavuma are the two openers for South Africa. Kasun Rajitha has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments from the start of the match but before that, both sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's​​​​​ first followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

Temba Bavuma, the captain of South Africa says they would have bowled first as well. Adds that they couldn't get the warm-up matches but the build up has been great and the home matches have put them in a good shape. Tells that adjusting to these conditions will be a challenge with bat and ball. Mentions that they have four pacers in Gerald Coetzee, Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen, ​and Lungi Ngidi. Says Keshav Maharaj is the specialist spinner while they are going with the normal top six for batting.

Sri Lanka's skipper Dasun Shanaka says that they will bowl first. Feels that there will be dew later on and therefore, they want to bowl first. Mentions that these are good tracks and they will look to restrict South Africa to as low as they can. Shares that the preparations have been really good apart from a few injuries. Informs that they are playing with three seamers and 8 batters including the three all-rounders.
